about: Sourced life stories for the prophets of the exile and the return (Ezekiel, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi, Shemaiah son of Delaiah and the prophetess Noadiah). Written from Scripture and the dossier Research/People/prophets-exile-return.md. Daniel's story is in prophets-exile.json.

ezekiel-ezk-1-3.short: Ezekiel the priest, son of Buzi, saw visions of God among the captives by the river Chebar and was made a watchman to the house of Israel.

paragraphs.text: Ezekiel was a priest, the son of Buzi. He was among the captives by the river Chebar in the land of the Chaldeans when, in the fifth year of king Jehoiachin's captivity, “the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God”. He saw the likeness of the glory of the LORD above four living creatures, and fell upon his face.

A voice sent him to the children of Israel, “a rebellious nation”, whether they would hear or forbear. He was given a roll written with lamentations and told to eat it, and it was in his mouth as honey. He came to the captives at Tel-abib and sat among them astonished seven days; then the LORD made him “a watchman unto the house of Israel”.

He lived in his own house among the exiles, and the elders came and sat before him. Many of his words were acted out before the people: he drew the siege of Jerusalem on a tile, lay on his side for many days, ate bread by weight, shaved his head and divided the hair, and carried his stuff out through a hole dug in the wall, as one going into captivity. In visions he was carried to Jerusalem and saw the glory of the LORD go up from the temple and from the city.

Ezekiel was married. The LORD told him he would take away “the desire of thine eyes with a stroke”, and that he must not mourn. He spoke to the people in the morning, his wife died at evening, and in the morning he did as he was commanded; he was to be a sign to them.

He had been told that his tongue would cleave to the roof of his mouth except when the LORD opened it. In the twelfth year of the captivity one who had escaped from Jerusalem came to him and said, “The city is smitten.” The evening before, the LORD had opened his mouth, and he was no more dumb. In the chapters that follow he speaks of a shepherd for the scattered flock, of a new heart, and of a valley of dry bones that lived again; in the twenty-fifth year he saw a new temple with a river flowing from under its threshold.
The latest date in his book is the twenty-seventh year. Scripture does not tell how or where Ezekiel died. His prophet page sets out his signs, visions and words.

haggai-ezr-5-1.short: Haggai the prophet urged the returned exiles to rebuild the house of the LORD in the second year of Darius, and the people obeyed his words.

paragraphs.text: Scripture gives Haggai no father, tribe or home. It calls him “Haggai the prophet” and “the LORD’s messenger in the LORD’s message”. His dated words all fall in the second year of Darius the king, and Ezra says that he and Zechariah the son of Iddo prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem.

On the first day of the sixth month the word of the LORD came by Haggai to Zerubbabel the governor of Judah and to Joshua the high priest. The people said the time had not come to build the LORD's house, while they dwelt in “cieled houses”. Haggai told them to go up to the mountain, bring wood and build. Zerubbabel, Joshua and the remnant of the people obeyed, and on the twenty-fourth day of the month they began the work.

In the seventh month he spoke to those who thought the new house as nothing beside the first: “be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the LORD, and work: for I am with you”. In the ninth month he asked the priests two questions about holy and unclean things, and on the same day the word came to him for Zerubbabel, that the LORD would make him as a signet.

Ezra says the elders of the Jews “prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo”, and finished the house in the sixth year of Darius. Scripture says nothing more of Haggai.

zechariah-ezr-5-1.short: Zechariah son of Berechiah saw night visions and prophesied with Haggai while the house of the LORD was rebuilt in the days of Darius.

paragraphs.text: Zechariah calls himself “the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo”; Ezra calls him “Zechariah the son of Iddo”. The word of the LORD came to him in the eighth month of the second year of Darius, calling the people to turn to the LORD and not to be as their fathers.

On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month he saw visions by night, and asked “the angel that talked with me” what they meant: a man on a red horse among myrtle trees, four horns, a man with a measuring line, Joshua the high priest clothed anew, a golden candlestick between two olive trees, a flying roll, a woman in an ephah, and four chariots.

In the vision of the candlestick a word came for Zerubbabel: “Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.” Zechariah was told to take silver and gold from Heldai, Tobijah and Jedaiah, who had come from Babylon, make crowns, and set them on the head of Joshua the high priest.

In the fourth year of Darius men were sent to ask whether they should still weep in the fifth month. The word came to Zechariah: execute true judgment and show mercy, and the fasts would become joy and gladness.

The rest of his book holds two burdens of the word of the LORD, among them the King who comes riding upon an ass, the thirty pieces of silver cast to the potter, and the day when the LORD shall be king over all the earth. The Gospels quote some of these words in telling of the last days of Jesus; Matthew gives one under the name of Jeremy the prophet.
Ezra says the elders “prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo” until the house was finished. Scripture does not tell how Zechariah's life ended.

malachi-mal-1-1.short: Malachi is known only from the heading of the book that bears his name, a word of the LORD to Israel.

paragraphs.text: Scripture tells nothing of Malachi beyond the heading of his book: “The burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi.” It gives him no father, home or date.

The book is a dispute. The LORD speaks, the people answer with a question, “Wherein?”, and the LORD replies. It rebukes priests who offer the blind and the lame, men who deal treacherously with the wife of their youth, and a people who have robbed God in tithes and offerings.

It promises a messenger to prepare the way, and ends with the call to remember the law of Moses and the promise, “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD”. Jesus said of John the Baptist, “this is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face”.

noadiah-neh-6-14.short: Noadiah, a prophetess, is named once, among the prophets who would have put Nehemiah in fear.

paragraphs.text: Noadiah is named only once. When Nehemiah had built the wall of Jerusalem and his enemies were plotting against him, he prayed: “My God, think thou upon Tobiah and Sanballat according to these their works, and on the prophetess Noadiah, and the rest of the prophets, that would have put me in fear.”

Just before, Nehemiah tells how Shemaiah the son of Delaiah had been hired by Tobiah and Sanballat to frighten him. He does not say whether Noadiah was hired, and Scripture records nothing she said and nothing more about her.

shemaiah-neh-6-10.short: Shemaiah son of Delaiah urged Nehemiah to hide in the temple; Nehemiah saw that God had not sent him and that his enemies had hired him.

paragraphs.text: Shemaiah was the son of Delaiah, the son of Mehetabeel. He is named only in Nehemiah 6, when Nehemiah had built the wall of Jerusalem and Sanballat and Geshem “thought to do me mischief”, as he writes.

Nehemiah came to his house, where Shemaiah “was shut up”. Shemaiah said, “Let us meet together in the house of God, within the temple, and let us shut the doors of the temple: for they will come to slay thee”. Nehemiah answered, “Should such a man as I flee?” and would not go in.

Nehemiah perceived “that God had not sent him”, but that Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him to make Nehemiah afraid and sin, so that they might have matter for an evil report. Scripture says no more of him.
